entries.note: Two fingers squeeze the wide button into a dot, then I loop a spinner in place for the wait and finish with a check where it turns green.
A single short flick to the right that shoots off fast and eases into its stop, the way the knob snaps across the track.
A rapid side-to-side scribble in place that loses amplitude each pass, like the field refusing and then settling.
A quick spiral that swells out and relaxes back for the heart's pop, then one fast ring thrown around it for the burst.
Two fingers pull opposite corners apart on a diagonal, moving quickly at first and gliding to a stop as the card fills the screen.
A quick drop from the top edge that settles and then just sits there for a long beat, followed by a fast lift back out of frame.
One upward push from the bottom edge that decelerates into its resting height, the way the sheet slides up and parks.
One finger walks the underline rightwards in two steps while the other drags the content the opposite way by the same two steps.
One short dash per row, each starting a beat after the last and stepping down the surface, for rows arriving one after another.
A small symmetric two-finger pop outward from the centre that goes a hair too far and eases back, since the dialog grows in place rather than travelling.
A slow, perfectly even ramp upward with no change of pace, standing for something that only gets stronger over time and never moves.
A straight line drawn left to right at one steady speed, matching the square's unchanging pace across the frame.
A fast run to the right that sails past the mark, swings back short and wobbles smaller each time before settling.
A vertical drop that speeds up into the floor, kicks back up a shorter distance, and does it once more smaller, hanging longest at the tops.
Two fingers spread apart from a single point, quick at the start and coasting to a halt, because the circle only ever grows and then holds.
One travelling loop: the path carries down to the right while curling through a full turn whose circle widens, so moving, spinning and growing are all in the one stroke.
One full clockwise circle drawn in place, easing in and out so the middle of the turn is the fastest part.
A sustained left-right zigzag on the spot, keeping roughly the same width the whole way instead of dying out.
A single smooth parabola from low left up over the top and down to low right, steep and quick at the ends and lingering at the peak.
